Theme

Kitchen, meals & drinks

pantry noun

also larder

classical

Traupman 124

cella penāria

Short e, as in penus: L&S pĕnārius.

Examples

  • Quid est hoc, tata? — Orȳza. — Quid hoc? — Collȳra.

    What’s this, Dad? — Rice. — What’s this? — Pasta.composed

  • Hae lentēs sunt; hae fabae, hoc cicer, haec farīna, hoc mel, hae ūvae passae.

    These are lentils; these are beans, this is chickpeas, this is flour, this is honey, these are raisins.composed

  • Hoc nesciō; aviam rogābimus.

    I don’t know this one; we’ll ask Grandma.composed

See also storeroom, rice, pasta, flour, store, pea.

SourcesLewis & Short: cella · Lewis & Short: penarius

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 70, 72, 124.
